title: This, that, someone
description: Point at things, and talk about people without naming them.

explanation.summary: Spanish has three words for this, depending on where the thing is, and four for that. It also has words that mean someone, nobody, something and nothing, and they behave like pronouns.

sections.heading: This and that
sections.body: Este means this, close to me. Ese means that, close to you. Aquello means that, far from both. And the neuter forms esto, eso and aquello point at a whole thing rather than a thing you could touch: esto es un restaurante, this is a restaurant.

examples.es: Esa casa es la de Ana.

examples.en: That over there is a castle.

sections.heading: Someone, nobody, something, nothing
sections.body: Alguien is someone, nadie is nobody, algo is something and nada is nothing. They are pronouns, so they take the verb directly: hay alguien, there is someone. The negative nada and nadie need a no in front: no hay nadie, there is nobody.

examples.en: There is someone in the kitchen.

sections.heading: Every, all, none
sections.body: Cada is every or each, and it goes before a noun: cada día, every day. Todo is all or everything: todo el mundo, everyone. Ninguno is none, and it agrees with the noun: ninguno de ellos, none of them.

examples.en: Every morning I read the newspaper.

exercises.prompt: Pair each word with its translation.
exercises.note: These words stand in for a noun: eso es mi coche. Alguien and nadie work the same way.
This, close to the speaker. It never changes.
That, close to the listener. It never changes.
